name: Evans Gambit — White Tactics
description: 4 tactical challenges for White in the Evans Gambit. Find the winning 2-move sequence from the critical position after 8...Bb6!

drills.name: The f7 Fork
drills.description: White launches the knight at f7, forking the queen and rook in one swoop.
drills.briefExplanation: White leaps to g5 threatening the devastating Nxf7 fork.
drills.explanation: After h6, Nxf7! is a royal fork — the knight simultaneously attacks the queen on d8 and the rook on h8. Black cannot save both pieces. If Qxf7, Bxf7+ wins a piece. If Rxf7 instead, the queen is still lost. White wins decisive material and maintains a powerful attack.

drills.name: Rook Activation + Pin
drills.description: White activates the rook on the e-file and immediately pins Black's developing knight.
drills.briefExplanation: Re1 loads the rook onto the e-file. When Black develops the knight to e7, Bg5 pins it immediately.
drills.explanation: Bg5 pins the Ne7 to the queen on d8. Black cannot move the knight without losing the queen. White combines the e-file pressure from Re1 with the powerful pin from Bg5, threatening Bxe7 and Nd5. Black is forced into a very passive position to untangle.

drills.name: Knight to the Outpost
drills.description: White develops the knight to c3 then immediately plants it on the dominant d5 square, attacking the bishop on b6.
drills.briefExplanation: Nc3 develops the knight, and when Black plays Nge7, Nd5 occupies the dominant outpost attacking the bishop on b6.
drills.explanation: The knight on d5 attacks the bishop on b6 directly. Black must either retreat the bishop (giving White a tempo) or accept that the knight dominates the entire center from d5. The d5 outpost is permanent — Black has no pawn that can challenge it. White follows with Bg5 or Re1, increasing the pressure.

drills.name: Bishop Sacrifice on f7
drills.description: White sacrifices the bishop on f7 to drag the Black king into the open, then delivers check with the knight.
drills.briefExplanation: Bxf7+ forces the king to capture, then Ng5+ puts it under immediate attack.
drills.explanation: After Kxf7, Ng5+ puts the king in check on f7. The king has no good square — Ke6 walks into Qd5+ with a decisive attack, Kg6 allows Qd3 threatening Qd5# and h4-h5, and Kf6 allows Qf3+ Ke7 Qf7#. White has sacrificed the bishop but unleashes a powerful attacking wave that Black cannot survive.
